To get a perfect SAT score, a student must answer all questions correctly. The SAT is scored based on the number of correct answers, so getting every question right is the only way to achieve a perfect score. Taking the test multiple times (option A) might improve your score, but it doesn't guarantee a perfect score. Studying all the time (option C), going to test prep (option E), or cheating (option D) are not guaranteed or ethical ways to get a perfect score. Remembering all the answers (option F) is unrealistic and not the intended method. Therefore, the correct answer is that the only way to get a perfect SAT score is to get all the questions right.

Answer: B
